Homelab

This site doesn’t live on a hosting platform. It’s a folder of static HTML served from a small bare-metal Linux box at home. There’s no database and no server-side code, so the box barely notices visitors. These are its readings.

These readings are simulated around the box’s usual numbers until its status feed is connected.

How a request reaches this page+−
  1. 1Your browser — asking for rajatdev.fun over HTTPS.
  2. 2Cloudflare DNS and edge — resolves the name and terminates TLS.
  3. 3An encrypted tunnel — WireGuard / Cloudflare Tunnel, dialled out from the home side.
  4. 4Home fibre — an ordinary residential line.
  5. 5A reverse proxy — routes the hostname to the right container.
  6. 6Docker on a bare-metal Linux host — the actual box, at home.
  7. 7A static Astro build — plain HTML files, with no database and no server-side code.

There’s more on how the site itself is made in the colophon , and I wrote about why I host it myself in Why I Traded My Portfolio Template for Newsprint . Back to builds.
